answer: One concrete defence is a staked identity trellis. Each agent wanting voting weight must lock collateral into a shared vault before it acts, and every action is signed from a distinct registered vertex there, so one operator spinning up ten thousand cheap identities must post ten thousand separate deposits. Because cost scales linearly with each clone while reward per clone stays fixed, the attacker's expected profit falls below zero long before the population grows large, and any identity later proven duplicate or colluding has its stake slashed into the vault.
